reason: Glandular-pilosulose means covered with minute pilose hairs, some of them gland-tipped. That falls under glandular-pubescent, defined as at least some hairs tipped with a gland. The fine hair length is not worth a separate class.
'Lacking spots' is the negation of PATO:0000333 spotted. 'fronts' in the source looks garbled, so the bearer needs checking.
'Anther dehiscence introrse' means the anther opens towards the centre of the flower, which is FLOPO:0991164 introrse. 'Introrse to latrorse' is a continuum.

'Pollen in monads' means the grains are shed singly, not in dyads, tetrads or polyads. The closest existing value is solitary (borne individually), but its definition is about attachment sites, so the fit is loose. A pollen dispersal-unit class would be better if dyads and tetrads become frequent.
Orbicular (PATO:0001934) with value_qualifier 'nearly'. 'Broadly ovate to nearly orbiculate' is also a continuum.
The quality is lanate (woolly). 'Sparsely' is a density adverb that stays in the record, as for 'sparsely pubescent'. 'infloresupinate' is a transcription fragment of the bearer, not of this word.

This is a length (PATO:0000122) of the male region of a spike or inflorescence (Carex, Cyperaceae). The bearer is that portion, with state male (PATO:0000384), using the part-of-the-bearer slot. It is a measurement, not a quality word.

The indumentum is hispidulous. The hairs being stellate (star shaped, PATO:0002065) is a quality of the hairs and can go on a second record. There is no stellate-hairy class yet, and 8 statements do not justify one.
A hyphenated compound read as a continuum between corymb-like (PATO:0002455, with 'sub' as an approximate qualifier) and raceme-like (FLOPO:0991197), as in the flora annotation playbook.
PATO:0001874 discoid has the exact synonyms disc-shaped and disk-shaped.
A movable (hinged) orchid lip has a disposition to move freely, which is PATO:0000299 mobile.

A raceme-like scorpioid cyme (Boraginaceae) is both scorpioid (FLOPO:0991179) and raceme-like (FLOPO:0991197). It is not a value between the two, so the continuum reading for hyphen compounds does not apply.
'Keel not extending to apex' relates a part of the sepal or bract (its keel, which is not the flower keel PO:0025327) to the apex, with a negation. It needs the relation pattern and the second part.
This is parallel to (PATO:0002272) towards the ventral side of the seed. It is a relational quality of the cotyledons with its second term given.
Same reading as 'parchment-like' in the previous review: parchment-like means papery, PATO:0104010 papyraceous.

label: torose
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cylindrical with slight swellings alternating with shallow constrictions along its length. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991168 moniliform, in which the constrictions are deep and the swellings bead-like; floras contrast the two ('torose to moniliform').
reason: A standard botanical shape term with no PATO or FLOPO term. Moniliform is the stronger degree and floras keep the two apart.
This is adnate (FLOPO:0991129) towards petiole (PO_0020038). 'For 1.5-2 mm' is a measurement of the fused length.
The stigma is square (PATO:0000413) and flattened (PATO:0002254) at the same time. This is a conjunction of two qualities, not one new value.
'Margin gland-fringed' means glands are present along the margin (part-of-the-bearer slot: margin). It contrasts with 'eglandular'. A presence rule is preferred to a new glandular-fringed term.
Patellate (patelliform) means like a small dish or kneecap. FLOPO:0991182 saucer-shaped already has the synonym patelliform.

Moss leaf cells with several papillae each are papillose. The number per cell (several, against one) is lost. Counting it with pattern 13 would need a part class for the cuticular papilla, which PO's papilla cell is not.
Bracts resembling the stem leaves are leaf-like: PATO:0002457, similar in appearance to a leaf.
'Apex thinly sharpened' (afilado) means drawn out to a sharp point. 'Not sharpened toward very base' (stipe) reads as tapered (PATO:0001500), so the rule should be limited to apex contexts.
This is recurved (PATO:0002211) with value_qualifier 'sub', as for 'suborbicular'.
A thinly walled fruit or monocarp has a thin pericarp. The quality is decreased thickness, with pericarp (PO_0009084) as the part of the bearer.

word: inserted above middle of calyx tube
reason: This is inserted into (PATO:0000624) towards the calyx tube, plus a position on it (above the middle). It is a relation with its second term, not a quality word.

'Culm leaved at base' means leaves are present on the basal part (part-of-the-bearer slot: base). 'Several leaved' is an indefinite count (pattern 13). Leafy (FLOPO:0991012) means leaves along the whole axis, which is not what these statements say.

'With 6 dark lines' and 'longitudinal dark lines' mean the part is marked by narrow, usually parallel lines, which is PATO:0001410 striated. Irregular streaks are FLOPO:0991206 streaked. The bare part sense 'line' stays rejected.
A hyphen compound read as a continuum between ovate (FLOPO:0991024) and triangular (PATO:0001875). 'Narrowly' is a modifier of the length-to-width ratio (pattern 11).
This negates PATO:0000333 spotted.
